what_its_for: Migalastat is used to treat Fabry disease in adults. Fabry disease is a rare inherited condition where your body cannot break down a certain type of fat called globotriaosylceramide (GL-3). This fat builds up in your organs and blood vessels and can cause serious problems. Migalastat works by helping a faulty enzyme in your body work better so it can break down this fat properly.
how_to_take: Swallow one capsule by mouth every other day (every 48 hours) — for example, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, and so on. Always take it on an empty stomach. Do not eat any food for at least 2 hours before taking the capsule AND at least 2 hours after taking it. Food can reduce how well this medicine works. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. Take it at the same time of day on your dosing days to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is one 123 mg capsule taken every other day (every 48 hours). Always follow your doctor's instructions. Do not take more than prescribed. Your doctor will have tested whether your specific type of Fabry disease is likely to respond to this medication before prescribing it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, check how much time has passed. If it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose on your regularly scheduled day. Never take two doses on the same day or within 24 hours of each other to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store migalastat capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original packaging until you are ready to use them. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use capsules past the expiration date printed on the package. Do not store in the bathroom, near a sink, or in damp or hot places.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat food for at least 2 hours before and 2 hours after taking your dose — this is very important. Avoid starting any new prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as some medicines may interact with migalastat. Talk to your doctor before drinking alcohol regularly while on this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a fast or irregular heartbeat or chest pain; shortness of breath or swelling in your legs or ankles (possible signs of heart problems); severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; unusual headaches or vision changes; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing; any new or worsening symptoms. Also call your doctor if you become pregnant or are planning to become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Migalastat does not cure Fabry disease, but it helps slow the buildup of harmful fats in your body over time. You may not notice immediate changes in how you feel — the medicine works gradually. Your doctor will check your progress with regular tests and appointments. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel well. It may take several months before your doctor can measure the full benefit of this medication.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of migalastat during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Kidney problems: Migalastat is not recommended if your kidneys are working at less than 30% of normal function (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²). Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Children: Migalastat is approved for adults aged 18 and older. It is not currently approved for use in children. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
